entries.title: II Samuel 2:1
segments:
Hebron; the chief city of Judah before David chose Jerusalem as his residence.  It lay in the central part of the territory of Judah, in a mountainous region; was an ancient and honorable city; and was every way suitable to be his residence while he reigned over Judah alone. 
 
Men who in all their ways acknowledge God, seek direction from him, and are disposed to follow his guidance, will see the path of duty, and in walking in it will find great reward.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:3
segments:
Cities of Hebron; towns near Hebron and dependent upon it. 
 
Those who have befriended and assisted us in adversity, should be gratefully remembered and duly honored by us in prosperity.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:4
segments:
Anointed David king; by the first anointing under Samuel's hand he had been designated by God as the future king; by the present anointing he was solemnly inducted into office. 
 
  Buried Saul;

entries.title: II Samuel 2:5
segments: Gratitude and kindness to benefactors are not only right, but the surest means of securing gratitude and kindness in return, and thus promoting the good of all concerned.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:8
segments:
Mahanaim; a city on the east of Jordan, in the tribe of Gad. 
 
Men who aspire to power, and grasp at the possession of it without asking counsel of God or inquiring whether it is right, though they may for a time succeed, will in the end find it to be a source of vexation, bitterness, and sorrow.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:9
segments: The Ashurites; supposed to have been a region east of the Jordan. It must not be confounded with the tribe of Asher.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:12
segments: Gibeon; north-west of Jerusalem, in the tribe of Benjamin.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:14
segments:
Play before us; the meaning of this proposal was, that a chosen number from each army should make a trial of their strength in fighting. 
 
Warriors often treat the butchering of men as a matter of sport, and thus show themselves to be children of him who was a murderer from the beginning, and who as a roaring lion walketh about seeking whom he may devour.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:16
segments: Helkath-hazzurim; meaning, according to some, the field of the strong men; according to others, the field of the swords.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:21
segments:
Take thee his armor; he means to say, that if Asahel is determined to fight, he should choose some one over whom he could prevail. 
 
Ambition to be distinguished as a warrior has often proved a man's ruin, and from the height of expectation and effort he has fallen suddenly into an untimely grave.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:26
segments:
Bitterness in the latter end; the unrelenting persecution of your brethren will exasperate them and drive them to extremities, and thus bring great calamities on you as well as on them. 
 
Want of success in war often disposes men to peace, and leads them to speak very differently about the evils of war from what they did when it began; and though they have been the cause of their own troubles, they often try to throw the blame of them on others.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:27
segments: Unless thou hadst spoken; that is, according to some, challenged the young men to combat,

.  Hadst thou in the morning of to-day shown a disposition for peace, my followers would have retired from thee in peace.  Others suppose him to mean, Unless thou hadst now spoken, the pursuit would not have ended till the morning of to-morrow. 
 
  Gone up; to the higher region of Hebron.

entries.title: II Samuel 2:29
segments: Bithron; a hilly country between the Jordan and Mahanaim.
